description_ru: Юмористический рассказ о походе с друзьями: неудачная палатка, мокрые спички, дождь в полночь и спасительный фермер.
text:
My friend Dave once told me that camping is "the perfect way to relax and enjoy nature". I have thought about this sentence many times since, usually at three o'clock in the morning, while lying in a wet sleeping bag and listening to the rain on a tent that I did not know how to put up. If I had understood what I was agreeing to, I would have stayed at home. Instead, I said yes, and last June I found myself in a field in the middle of nowhere with three friends and a bag of sausages.

The trip began badly. We drove for four hours, and when we arrived, it was already starting to get dark. Dave, who had promised that he was an expert, opened the bag that contained the tent and stared at it for a long time. "It is different from the one I borrowed last time," he said slowly. There were poles, ropes, small metal pegs and a big piece of green cloth that smelled like a damp dog. We tried for an hour to understand the instructions, and in the end we built something that looked like a collapsed circus.

Our second problem was the fire. Everyone knows that camping means sitting around a fire, singing songs and eating food. My friend Sasha had brought a small box of matches, and we collected sticks from the nearby trees. Unfortunately, the sticks were wet, and the matches were wetter. We tried to burn paper, then a few leaves, and finally a packet of biscuits, which did produce a small flame but also a terrible smell. After forty minutes, we gave up and ate our sausages cold, which was not as good as the pictures suggested.

By ten o'clock we were exhausted, and we crawled into the tent. I discovered that a sleeping bag is a kind of plastic bag with a zip, and that the ground, which looks soft in the daytime, becomes as hard as a table at night. Dave started snoring almost at once, and Sasha, who was lying next to him, kept hitting him with a shoe. I could not sleep. Every little noise seemed enormous: a leaf, a branch, something that I was sure was a bear. When I mentioned this, Dave woke up and told me that there were no bears in this country. "Then what is that?" I asked. "Probably a cow," he said, and went back to sleep.

The rain started at midnight. At first it was gentle, but soon it was loud and heavy, and I noticed a small, cold drop falling on my nose. Then another. Because Dave had put the tent too close to a hill, a river of water began to run underneath us, and my sleeping bag slowly turned into a sponge. By two o'clock we were all sitting up, wrapped in blankets and holding torches. Sasha said that if somebody had told her that this was a holiday, she would have asked for her money back. We laughed so hard that we forgot to be cold.

At dawn the rain stopped, and we came out of the tent to discover a beautiful morning. The sun was rising over the hills, the grass was shining and a family of ducks was walking across the field. For a moment I understood what Dave had meant. It was truly lovely. Then I noticed that the ducks were walking on my shoe, which I had left outside, and that one of them was trying to eat my sock. It was very hard to feel peaceful while chasing a bird across a field in my pyjamas.

Breakfast was a success, mainly because the farmer who owned the field arrived with a basket of eggs and bread. He looked at our collapsed tent, shook his head and offered to cook for us on his own stove. "You are the third group this month," he said kindly. "The last people tried to build a fire in the bathroom." We sat at his kitchen table and ate eggs, toast and bacon, and I have never enjoyed a meal so much. Nothing tastes better than food that someone else has made after a night in the rain.

We drove home in the afternoon, tired, dirty and happy. I have not forgiven Dave, but I admit that it was the best weekend I have had for years. Already, he has suggested another trip for the autumn. This time, he says, he will buy a new tent, a proper stove and a book about survival. I told him that I would think about it. If it rains again, I have decided, I will be the one who stays in the farmer's kitchen.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Кончик языка слегка между зубами, воздух проходит без голоса; не заменяйте на «с» или «ф».
Губы округлены и вытянуты вперёд, зубов не касаются; это не русское «в».
Спинка языка прижата к нёбу, звук идёт через нос; в конце -ing не добавляйте «г».
В конце слова и перед согласной «l» твёрдое: кончик языка вверху, спинка оттянута назад.

questions.question: What was wrong with the tent?
questions.answer: Dave could not understand how to build it, and it ended up like a collapsed circus.

questions.question: Why could they not cook the sausages?
questions.answer: The sticks and the matches were wet, so they could not make a fire.

questions.question: What kept the narrator awake at night?
questions.answer: Strange noises, then the rain and the water under the tent.

questions.question: Who saved their breakfast?
questions.answer: The farmer brought eggs and bread and cooked in his kitchen.
